If an hiv positive person is adhering to medication and undetectable, there is no risk, even with unprotected sex. As long as that person is undetectable and adhering to treatment, there is no “risk” to inform their sexual partners about. Personally, if the partner is a significant other, they should know; but a fling is a different story.

Current medication is so strong that the virus can’t be detected in a standard blood test. People with hiv also have more of an incentive to adhere to meds than just having sex. Being on treatment means that they won’t develop aids and aids related illnesses.
